# TypeLua — full reference (EN, self-contained)

> Generated from docs/en/*.md. Every ```typelua block passes `tlua check`.

# TypeLua

> TypeLua is a typed superset of Lua (TypeScript-for-Lua). Types erase to idiomatic Lua (5.4 default, 5.1/LuaJIT compatible). Only `class`/`enum` emit runtime values.

- [Docs home](https://github.com/types-lua/docs): bilingual guides (EN/ZH) + full references
- [SPEC v0.8](https://github.com/types-lua/TypeLua/blob/main/SPEC.md): normative language contract, §§1–16
- [Examples](https://github.com/types-lua/TypeLua/tree/main/examples): 25 runnable `tlua check`-clean programs
- [Diagnostics](https://github.com/types-lua/TypeLua/blob/main/internal/diag/codes.go): stable `TLxxxx` registry
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/types-lua/TypeLua/blob/main/AGENTS.md): agent bootstrap for the compiler repo

## Guide (site: https://types-lua.github.io/docs/)

- [Index](https://types-lua.github.io/docs/en/): what/why, doc map
- [Quickstart](https://types-lua.github.io/docs/en/01-quickstart): init/check/build/run in 5 minutes
- [Language](https://types-lua.github.io/docs/en/02-language): types, declarations, narrowing, classes, generics
- [CLI & Tooling](https://types-lua.github.io/docs/en/03-cli): tlua.json, `--format=json`, packages, LSP
- [Concurrency](https://types-lua.github.io/docs/en/04-concurrency): defer, coroutines, async/spawn/chan/select
- [FFI & Native](https://types-lua.github.io/docs/en/05-ffi): ffi, bindgen, shims, .d.tl, assets
- [Patterns & Fixes](https://types-lua.github.io/docs/en/06-patterns): recipes + TL error-fix table
- [Testing](https://types-lua.github.io/docs/en/07-testing): `tlua test`, assertions, CI recipe
- [Examples](https://types-lua.github.io/docs/en/08-examples): `tlua example`, cargo-style runs
- [Debugging](https://types-lua.github.io/docs/en/09-debugging): `tlua dap`, breakpoints, Test Explorer

## Quickstart

```bash
go build -o tlua ./cmd/tlua
./tlua init
./tlua check --format=json
./tlua build
./tlua run --check main.tl
```

```lua
type Point = { x: number, y: number }
local function dist(a: Point, b: Point): number
  local dx: number = a.x - b.x
  local dy: number = a.y - b.y
  return dx * dx + dy * dy
end
local p: Point = { x = 1, y = 2 }
print(dist(p, { x = 4, y = 6 }))
```

## Testing (zero config)

```
tlua test
tlua test --filter NAME --format=json
tlua test --lua luajit --target 5.1
```

A test file returns named cases and imports the injected helper:

```lua
import T from "tlua_test"
return {
  ["adds"] = function(): void T.eq(1 + 1, 2) end,
}
```

## Examples (cargo style)

```
tlua example              # list examples/*.tl and examples/*/main.tl
tlua example basic -- a   # run with arguments
```

The first `---` line of an example is its description.

## Debugging

```
tlua dap                    # stdio DAP; VS Code drives it for F5/tests
tlua test --list --format=json
```

Needs an external `lua5.4`/`luajit`; pause-while-running and evaluate are not
supported.

## Rules

- Valid Lua 5.4 is valid TypeLua; `type`/`class`/`import`/`defer`/`await`/`spawn`/`select`/`async`/`macro` are contextual.
- `strictNilChecks` is on: narrow with `==nil`/`~=nil`, `type(x)==`, `=="lit"`, truthiness, member paths.
- `interface` is structural, `class` instances are nominal; `super(...)` only in derived constructors before `self`.
- `import N from "p"` is typed `require` sugar; `import N from "./x"` is a package-local import, emitted as a stable module name (`lib.codec`, `example.com.pkg.codec`); `require("./x")` is `TL4002`.
- `require("ffi")` is typed only when `require` is not shadowed.
- `defer f()` takes a call, LIFO at function exit; `errdefer` only on explicit `error()` in the same function.
- Concurrency is single-threaded CSP: `await`/`select` outside `async` is `TL3801`/`TL3802`; sync callers cannot call blocking primitives (`TL3805`).
- FFI/`.so` needs `--target 5.1` + `--lua luajit`; `ffi.cdef` is opaque, hand-write `as CLib`; `.d.tl` checks but never emits.
- JSON diags: `{file,line,column,endLine,endColumn,severity,code,category,message}`; `code` is stable.

## tlua.json

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": { "target": "5.4", "strict": true, "outDir": "dist", "rootDir": "." },
  "include": ["**/*.tl"],
  "exclude": ["dist"]
}
```

Full reference: `https://types-lua.github.io/docs/llms-full.txt`. Chinese: `https://types-lua.github.io/docs/llms-zh.txt` (concise), `https://types-lua.github.io/docs/llms-full-zh.txt` (full).

# TypeLua — English index

> TypeLua is Lua with erasable static types (TypeScript-for-Lua). Default target Lua 5.4, compatible with 5.1/LuaJIT. `class`/`enum` are the only type-level constructs with runtime values.

## Reading order

1. `en/index.md` — what/why, doc map (read first)
2. `en/01-quickstart.md` — init/check/build/run in 5 minutes
3. `en/02-language.md` — types, declarations, narrowing, classes, generics
4. `en/03-cli.md` — `tlua.json`, CLI flags, `--format=json`, LSP, diagnostics
5. `en/04-concurrency.md` — `defer`, coroutines, `async`/`await`/`spawn`/`chan`/`select`
6. `en/05-ffi.md` — FFI, `bindgen`, cross-language shims, `.d.tl`, packaging
7. `en/06-patterns.md` — agent recipes + error-fix table

## Minimal program (verified)

```typelua
type Point = { x: number, y: number }
local function dist(a: Point, b: Point): number
  local dx: number = a.x - b.x
  local dy: number = a.y - b.y
  return dx * dx + dy * dy
end
local p: Point = { x = 1, y = 2 }
print(dist(p, { x = 4, y = 6 }))
```

## tlua.json (sane default)

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": { "target": "5.4", "strict": true, "outDir": "dist", "rootDir": "." },
  "include": ["**/*.tl"],
  "exclude": ["dist"]
}
```

## Agent commands

```bash
go build -o tlua ./cmd/tlua
./tlua check --format=json
./tlua build
./tlua run --check main.tl
```

Full reference: `llms-full.txt`. Chinese: `llms-zh.txt` / `llms-full-zh.txt`.
Contract: `https://github.com/types-lua/TypeLua/blob/main/SPEC.md`.

<!-- docs/en/01-quickstart.md -->

# Quickstart (EN)

## 1. Install and scaffold

```bash
go build -o tlua ./cmd/tlua
./tlua init
./tlua check
./tlua build   # -> dist/*.lua
./tlua run main.tl -- arg1 arg2
```

`./tlua init` writes `tlua.json` plus a hello `main.tl` when missing.
`./tlua check` prints `checked N file(s): no errors` and exits 1 on error.
`./tlua build --watch` (or `./tlua watch`) recompiles on change like `tsc --watch`.

## 2. Your first typed program

```typelua
type Point = { x: number, y: number }
local function dist(a: Point, b: Point): number
  local dx: number = a.x - b.x
  local dy: number = a.y - b.y
  return dx * dx + dy * dy
end
local p: Point = { x = 1, y = 2 }
print(dist(p, { x = 4, y = 6 }))
```

Run it without leaving artifacts:

```bash
./tlua run --check main.tl
```

Expected output is `25`.

## 3. Target 5.4 vs 5.1

Default `target` is `5.4`. Use `5.1` for LuaJIT:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": { "target": "5.1", "strict": true, "outDir": "dist", "rootDir": "." },
  "include": ["**/*.tl"],
  "exclude": ["dist"]
}
```

`--target 5.1` strips `<const>`/`<close>` and hides
`coroutine.close`/`coroutine.isyieldable`. FFI and `.so` modules always need
`--target 5.1` plus an external interpreter:

```bash
./tlua build --target 5.1
./tlua run --target 5.1 --lua luajit main.tl
```

The embedded `run` (golua) cannot load C modules by design.

## 4. Nil safety from the start

```typelua
local function greet(name: string | nil): string
  if name == nil then
    return "hello, stranger"
  end
  return "hello, " .. name
end
print(greet(nil))
print(greet("ada"))
```

`strictNilChecks` is on by default: `nil` is not assignable to `string`.
Narrow with `==nil`/`~=nil`, `type(x)`, `=="lit"`, truthiness, or member paths:

```typelua
type Node = { v: number, next: Node | nil }
local function head(n: Node | nil): number
  if n == nil then
    return 0
  end
  if n.next then
    return n.next.v
  end
  return n.v
end
print(head(nil))
print(head({ v = 7, next = { v = 8, next = nil } }))
```

## 5. Next steps

- Language details: `en/02-language.md`
- CLI + JSON diags + LSP: `en/03-cli.md`
- If `tlua check` fails, read the `TLxxxx` code in the fix table (`en/06-patterns.md`).


<!-- docs/en/02-language.md -->

# Language reference (EN)

Covers SPEC §§2–6 + §8 essentials. Every snippet checks clean.

## Types

```typelua
local a: any = 1
local u: unknown = "s"
local n: number = 1.5
local i: integer = 3
local f: float = 1.5
local s: string = "hi"
local b: boolean = true
local t: table = {}
local lit: "red" = "red"
local num: 42 = 42
local arr: number[] = { 1, 2, 3 }
local m: map<string, number> = { alice = 3 }
local tup: [string, number] = { "age", 30 }
local uni: number | nil = nil
type Both = { a: number } & { b: string }
local inter: Both = { a = 1, b = "x" }
local opt: string? = nil
print(a, u, n, i, f, s, b, #arr, m.alice, tup[1], uni, inter, opt)
```

`integer`/`float` are subtypes of `number`. `T?` means `T | nil`.
`map<K, V>` field access requires `K` to accept `string` for dot access.
`keyof`/`typeof`/indexed access/conditionals are in Advanced below.

## Type aliases, interfaces, enums

```typelua
type Point = { x: number, y: number }
type List<T> = { head: T, tail: List<T> | nil }
interface Named { name: string, greet(msg: string): string }
interface Employee extends Named { id: integer }
enum Color { Red = "red", Green = "green", Blue = "blue" }
enum N { A, B = 5, C }
local p: Point = { x = 1, y = 2 }
local c: Color = Color.Red
local e: Employee = {
  name = "bo",
  id = 7,
  greet = function(msg: string): string return msg .. "bo" end,
}
print(p.x, c, e.id, N.C)
```

Mixed string enums need explicit values on every member after the first
(`TL3120` otherwise). `interface` is structural; class instances are nominal.

## Functions (both type syntaxes work)

```typelua
local function add(a: number, b: number): number return a + b end
local function divmod(a: number, b: number): (number, number) return a / b, a % b end
local function cat(...nums: number[]): string
  local out: string = ""
  for _, v in ipairs(nums) do out = out .. tostring(v) end
  return out
end
local q: number
local r: number
q, r = divmod(7, 2)
print(add(2, 3), q, r, cat(1, 2, 3))
```

Multi-return is `-> (A, B)`; only the last call in an argument list expands.
Generic functions infer, or take explicit arguments:

```typelua
local function id<T>(v: T): T return v end
local function first<T>(xs: T[]): T | nil
  if #xs == 0 then return nil end
  return xs[1]
end
print(id<string>("hi"), id<number>(7), first<string>({ "a", "b" }))
print(first<number>({}))
```

Explicit args also work on methods and constructors: `obj:m<T>()`, `C.new<T>()`.

## Narrowing (nil-safe Lua)

```typelua
local function use(x: number | string | nil): string
  if x == nil then
    return "none"
  end
  if type(x) == "string" then
    return "str:" .. x
  end
  return "num:" .. tostring(x + 1)
end
print(use(nil))
print(use("hi"))
print(use(41))
```

Truthiness also narrows (`if x then` drops `nil`/`false`), and member paths
narrow without a temporary:

```typelua
type Node = { v: number, next: Node | nil }
local function second(n: Node): number
  if n.next then
    return n.next.v
  end
  return n.v
end
print(second({ v = 1, next = { v = 2, next = nil } }))
```

`x as T` passes when either direction is assignable; `x!` strips `nil`;
`!=` is `~=` and always emits as `~=`.

## Classes (nominal, block-scoped)

```typelua
abstract class Animal {
  name: string,
  constructor(name: string) self.name = name end,
  abstract speak(): string,
  describe(): string return "i am " .. self.name end,
}
class Dog extends Animal {
  tricks: string[] = {},
  static count: integer = 0,
  constructor(name: string) super(name) end,
  speak(): string return "woof" end,
}
local d = Dog.new("rex")
print(d:describe(), d:speak())
```

Rules: single `extends` + multiple `implements`; subclass instances assign to
base, unrelated classes never mix; `private`/`protected`/`readonly`/`static`/
`abstract` are compile-time; `super(...)` only in derived constructors before
`self`, `super:m(...)` for base methods; abstract classes cannot be
instantiated. Declare-only classes (`declare class`) emit nothing.

## Advanced types (conditional / keyof / indexed / mapped)

```typelua
type IsString<T> = T extends string ? true : false
type Head<T> = T extends [infer H, ...unknown[]] ? H : never
type NameOf<T> = keyof T
local a: IsString<string> = true
local h: Head<[string, number]> = "first"
type P = { x: number, y?: string, readonly z: boolean }
local k: NameOf<P> = "x"
local px: P[string] = 1
type RO<T> = { readonly [K in keyof T]: T[K] }
print(a, h, k, px)
```

`infer` only appears inside an `extends` clause. Bare type parameters
distribute over unions. Indexed access requires every key to exist
(`TL3603`). `keyof` mappings inherit optionality/readonly unless `-?`/
`-readonly` forces the opposite. Recursive aliases must go through an object
(`type A = A` is `TL3106`).

## Imports are typed requires

```typelua
-- math_utils.tl
local M: { double(n: number): number } = {
  double = function(n: number): number return n * 2 end,
}
return M
```

```typelua
-- main.tl
import U from "math_utils"
print(U.double(21))
```

The checker infers the module type from `return M`; annotate the boundary
(`import U: T from "p"` or `require(...) as T`) to freeze it. Mismatches are
`TL3010`. Missing/circular/self imports degrade to `any`, never to a crash.


## Relative imports (package-local)

Multi-file libraries can import siblings without touching `package.path`:
a path starting with `./` or `../` resolves against the **requiring file**
(`x.tl`, then `x/init.tl`).

```typelua
-- FILE: lib/codec.tl
local M: { add(a: number, b: number): number } = {
  add = function(a: number, b: number): number return a + b end,
}
return M

-- FILE: lib/init.tl
import codec from "./codec"
local M: { add(a: number, b: number): number } = { add = codec.add }
return M

-- FILE: main.tl
import L from "./lib"
print(L.add(1, 2))
```

The emitter rewrites the import to a stable module name: relative to the
project root (`lib.codec`) or, for vendored packages, to `tlua_modules/`
(`example.com.pkg.codec`). A directory import canonicalizes `pkg/init.tl` to
`pkg`, so `require("pkg")` elsewhere addresses the same module instance.

Rules and diagnostics:

- Targets must be non-declaration `.tl` files inside the project root.
- Missing targets, paths escaping the root, `.d.tl` targets and module-name
  collisions (`a.b.tl` vs `a/b.tl`) are `TL4002`.
- `require("./x")` has no relative semantics and is rejected with the same
  code; use `import Name from "./x"` instead.

## Macros are hygienic

```typelua
macro twice(x) = (x) + (x)
macro unless(cond, body) do
  if not (cond) then
    body
  end
end
local v: number = twice(20) + 1
unless(v == 0, print("nonzero"))
print(v)
```

Expression macros use `=`, statement macros use `do ... end`. Parameters are
renamed per expansion (hygiene); statement macros in expression position are
`TL3704`; arity must match (`TL3702`); trailing `...` must be last and only
splices into call args (`TL3706`).


<!-- docs/en/03-cli.md -->

# CLI & Tooling (EN)

## tlua.json

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "5.4",
    "strict": true,
    "strictNilChecks": true,
    "noImplicitAny": false,
    "outDir": "dist",
    "rootDir": ".",
    "sourceMap": false,
    "treeShake": false,
    "types": [],
    "typeRoots": ["types", "tlua_modules/@types"]
  },
  "include": ["**/*.tl"],
  "exclude": ["dist"]
}
```

`types: []` means all ambient `.d.tl` files (mirrors `tsconfig.types`).
`typeRoots` defaults are `types` + `tlua_modules/@types`; missing dirs are ignored.
`.d.tl` files check but never emit.

## Commands

```bash
./tlua init
./tlua check
./tlua check --format=json
./tlua build --target 5.1 --treeShake
./tlua build --format=json
./tlua run main.tl -- arg1 arg2
./tlua run --check --format=json main.tl
./tlua run --lua luajit --target 5.1 main.tl
./tlua watch
./tlua bindgen --header foo.h --out types/foo.d.tl --shim foo.tl
./tlua lsp
```

`check`/`build`/`run --check` accept `--format=text|json` (default `text`,
exit code unchanged). `watch` stays text (streaming logs). `--target` only
accepts `5.4`/`5.1`. `build` with no `.tl` files is `no .tl files found`.

## JSON diagnostics (for agents)

```bash
./tlua check --format=json
```

```json
[
  {
    "file": "bad.tl",
    "line": 1,
    "column": 7,
    "endLine": 1,
    "endColumn": 8,
    "severity": "error",
    "code": "TL3010",
    "category": "checker",
    "message": "type '\"oops\"' is not assignable to type 'number'"
  }
]
```

Keys are stable and sorted by file/line/column. `code` ranges:
`TL1xxx` lexer, `TL2xxx` parser, `TL3xxx` checker, `TL37xx` macros,
`TL38xx` concurrency, `TL4xxx` project. `category` derives from the code.

## Packages

```bash
./tlua mod init
./tlua mod get example.com/greet@v1.2.0
./tlua mod fetch
./tlua mod vendor
./tlua mod list
./tlua mod graph
```

Modules are git repos addressed by path (`github.com/owner/repo[/sub]`),
pinned in `tlua.toml`/`tlua.lock` (MVS, `exact` pins, `replace` for local
paths). `vendor` copies `*.tl` into `tlua_modules/<path>/`; builds emit
`tlua_modules/**/*.tl` to `dist/tlua_modules/...` and inject a bootstrap
prelude so `lua dist/main.lua` runs without `LUA_PATH` setup.

A typed dependency boundary looks like this:

```typelua
-- math_utils.tl
local M: { double(n: number): number } = {
  double = function(n: number): number return n * 2 end,
}
return M
```

```typelua
-- main.tl
import U from "math_utils"
print(U.double(21))
```

## Examples

`tlua example` lists `examples/*.tl` and `examples/*/main.tl` and runs one by
name (see [Examples](./08-examples)).

```bash
tlua example
tlua example basic --check
tlua example basic --lua lua5.4
```

## Testing

`tlua test` discovers `tests/**`, type-checks the project, injects the
`tlua_test` helper and runs every named case (see [Testing](./07-testing)).

```bash
tlua test
tlua test --filter store --format=json
tlua test --lua lua5.4
```

## Debugging

`tlua dap` is a stdio Debug Adapter Protocol server; the VS Code extension
starts it for `F5`/Test Explorer debugging (see [Debugging](./09-debugging)).

```bash
tlua dap
tlua test --list --format=json
```

## LSP (stdio)

```bash
./tlua lsp
```

Incremental sync (`textDocumentSync: 2`), hover, definition, completion on
`.`/`:` (members included), references, rename, document symbols. Diagnostics
push as `textDocument/publishDiagnostics` with `{range, severity, code,
source: "tlua", message}`. Diagnostics load ambient `.d.tl` declarations
from the nearest `tlua.json` (`typeRoots`). Cross-file import types are still
single-file, so `tlua check` is authoritative for project-wide inference.

## sourceMap and treeShake

```bash
./tlua build --sourceMap
./tlua build --treeShake
```

`--sourceMap` writes `<out>.lua.map` (V3 + `sourcesContent`) plus a
`--# sourceMappingURL=` footer. `--treeShake` drops zero-reference pure local
functions (`local function f` / single `local x = function`, transitive).
Globals, methods, table fields, `require`/`import`, `return`-reachable and
multi-value/attributed locals are never removed. Unknown AST nodes disable
shaking for that file (fail-safe).


<!-- docs/en/04-concurrency.md -->

# Concurrency (EN)

Single-threaded CSP on coroutines: no true parallelism. `async`/`await` are
explicit markers that erase to plain calls.

## defer / errdefer (LIFO cleanup)

```typelua
local function read(name: string): number
  local log: { close(): void } = {
    close = function(): void print("close", name) end,
  }
  local function closeLog(): void log.close() end
  defer closeLog()
  if name == "" then
    return 0
  end
  return 1
end
print(read("a"))
print(read(""))
```

`defer f()` / `errdefer f()` take a call, run LIFO at function exit, and
capture lazily (Lua closure rules). `errdefer` runs only when the same
function leaves via an explicit `error(...)`. Never pass bare `...`
(`TL3235`).

## Coroutines (typed)

```typelua
local co: thread = coroutine.create(function()
  coroutine.yield("step")
end)
local ok: boolean
local v: any
ok, v = coroutine.resume(co)
print(ok, v)
print(coroutine.status(co))
```

`create` requires a function (`TL3233`); `resume` returns `(boolean, any)`;
`running()` returns `(thread, boolean | nil)`; `close`/`isyieldable` exist
only on 5.4 (`TL3203` on 5.1). Literal `status(co) == "dead"` narrows.

## async / await + spawn + chan + select

```typelua
local jobs: chan<integer> = makeChan<integer>(4)
local done: chan<boolean> = makeChan<boolean>(1)

async function worker(): void
  while true do
    local v: integer
    local ok: boolean
    v, ok = await jobs:recv()
    if not ok then
      await done:send(true)
      return
    end
    print("did", v)
  end
end

async function main(): void
  spawn worker()
  await jobs:send(1)
  await jobs:send(2)
  jobs:close()
  local d: boolean
  local ok2: boolean
  d, ok2 = await done:recv()
  print("done", d, ok2)
end

await main()
```

Rules agents trip on:

- `await`/`select` only inside `async` functions or the top-level chunk
  (`TL3801`/`TL3802`).
- Sync functions cannot call `async` functions or blocking primitives
  (`sleep`/`timeout`, `ch:send`/`ch:recv`, `wg:wait`, `mu:lock`) — `TL3805`.
  `spawn` is exempt.
- `chan<T>` is invariant; `makeChan<T>(cap?)` must spell `T` (`TL3803`).
- `recv()` returns `(T, boolean)` (`ok=false` when closed and drained);
  `send` on a closed channel errors; `close` twice errors.
- `select` uses braces with `case` guards and optional trailing `default`:

```typelua
local ch: chan<integer> = makeChan<integer>(1)
await ch:send(9)
select {
  case local v = ch:recv() then
    print("got", v)
  case timeout(5.0) then
    print("timed out")
  default then
    print("busy")
}
```

Only `recv`/`send`/`timeout`/`sleep` guards are allowed. First ready case in
source order wins (not random). `break` exits the select; `return`/`defer`
behave normally. `for v in ch:iter() do` drains until close but cannot wait
inside `--target 5.1` iterators.

`WaitGroup`/`Mutex` follow Go spelling (`new`/`add`/`done`/`wait`,
`new`/`lock`/`unlock`/`tryLock`) with `await` on `wait`/`lock`.


<!-- docs/en/05-ffi.md -->

# FFI & Native (EN)

FFI needs LuaJIT: `--target 5.1` plus `--lua luajit`. The checker accepts FFI
types on 5.4 too, so snippets below still `check` clean everywhere.

## Direct FFI (explicit boundary)

```typelua
local ffi = require("ffi")
ffi.cdef[[
  int add(int a, int b);
]]
type CLib = { add(a: integer, b: integer): integer }
local C = ffi.load("mylib") as CLib
local n: number = C.add(20, 22)
print(n)
```

- `cdata`/`ctype` never mix with `userdata` (`TL3010`; dubious conversions
  are `TL3204`).
- `cdef` strings are opaque and emitted verbatim; the author guarantees the C
  side. The type boundary is always hand-written `as CLib`.
- If the local `require` is shadowed, `require("ffi")` degrades to `any`
  (old code keeps working).

## bindgen (header is the single source)

```bash
tlua bindgen --header mylib.h --out types/mylib.d.tl --shim mylib.tl --lib MyLib
```

Generates a `type`/enum/`interface` contract plus an optional typed shim
(`require ffi` + `cdef` + script-dir `ffi.load` + single `as` + `return`).
Callers then `import` with zero casts. Point `--so` at the real shared object
when the filename differs from `lib<base>.so`.

## Cross-language shim (one mouth)

Hide the three shapes (C module / FFI-direct / shim process) behind
`require` + `.d.tl`:

```typelua
-- native_shim.lua (HOW, plain Lua kept next to the .tl)
local M = {}
function M.native_add(a, b) return a + b end
return M
```

```typelua
-- native.d.tl (WHAT, checks but never emits)
declare type NativeLib = { native_add(a: number, b: number): number }
```

```typelua
-- main.tl (caller only sees require + as; in a real project NativeLib
-- comes from native.d.tl, here it is spelled locally so the file checks alone)
type NativeLib = { native_add(a: number, b: number): number }
local M = require("native_shim") as NativeLib
print(M.native_add(20, 22))
```

The recommended shape (`examples/c`) is: `.h` → `bindgen` → `.d.tl` → one
hand-written TypeLua shim (`cdef` + `ffi.load` + single `as`, ends with
`return M`) → callers `import C from "mylib"` with no casts.

## Assets and packaging

`build` passes through `*.lua` shims, `*.so`/`*.dylib`/`*.dll`, and `*.a`
into `dist` (same layout). `mod vendor` copies all four kinds into
`tlua_modules/<path>/`. `.a` never enters `package.cpath`: link it into the
host binary and call it via `ffi.C` instead of `ffi.load`. Keep headers and
docs out of `vendor` (cache only).

Watch tracks `ListNativeAssets` (`.lua`/`.so`/`.a` changes rebuild); `outDir`
is never watched.


<!-- docs/en/06-patterns.md -->

# Patterns & Fixes (EN)

## Wrap legacy Lua with a typed boundary

```typelua
-- legacy.lua returns an untyped table; keep it plain Lua.
-- legacy.tl (typed facade next to it)
local raw = require("legacy") as any
type Legacy = { parse(s: string): number }
local L = raw as Legacy
local n: number = L.parse("42")
print(n)
```

Prefer `as` at one place and export the `Legacy` type; don't sprinkle `any`.

## Module pattern (inferred, frozen at the edge)

```typelua
-- greet.tl
local Greet: { hello(name: string): string } = {
  hello = function(name: string): string return "hi " .. name end,
}
return Greet
```

```typelua
-- main.tl
import G from "greet"
print(G.hello("bo"))
```

If the boundary changes incompatibly, pin it explicitly
(`import G: Api from "greet"`) to get `TL3010` at the edge instead of
surprises inside.

## Error-fix table (what agents hit most)

| Code | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `TL2015` | Nesting > 256 | Split the expression/type/block; don't hand-nest 200+ deep. |
| `TL3010` | Not assignable | Add a narrow (`==nil`, `type(x)==`, `as T`) or fix the boundary `as`. |
| `TL3001` | Duplicate type | Ambient `.d.tl` + local share a name; rename the local. |
| `TL3103` | Undefined type | Import the file or add the `.d.tl`; check `types` allowlist. |
| `TL3106` | Recursive/over-deep generic | Route recursion through an object; avoid `L<L<T>>`-style self-feeding. |
| `TL3201` | Undefined variable | Declare before use; `self` only in methods. |
| `TL3203` | No such field | Narrow the union first; check `keyof`/optional (`?`). |
| `TL3232`/`TL3233` | Arity/type mismatch | Count args (methods pass `self`); match `(A, B)` multi-return. |
| `TL3234` | Bad explicit type args | Fill missing slots left-to-right; respect `extends` constraints. |
| `TL3310` | Visibility | `private` only inside the class; don't reach through instances for `static`. |
| `TL3602`/`TL3603` | Bad mapped/indexed access | Map only over literal-union/`keyof`/index-signature domains; ensure keys exist. |
| `TL37xx` | Macro misuse | Arity exact; statement macro stays in statement position; `...` last and only into call args. |
| `TL3801`/`TL3802` | `await`/`select` outside async | Mark the function `async` or move to the chunk top level. |
| `TL3805` | Sync calls async/blocking | `spawn` it, or make the caller `async` and `await` it. |
| `TL4001` | Cannot read file | Fix `include`/`exclude`/`rootDir`; `outDir` is never an input. |

## 5.1 checklist

- No `<const>`/`<close>`, no `//`, no bitwise ops, no `goto` into new scoping.
- `coroutine.close`/`isyieldable` don't exist (`TL3203`).
- `yield` cannot cross `pcall` or for-iterators; move the suspension out.
- FFI/`.so` runs need `--lua luajit`, never embedded `run`.

## Agent workflow (cheap → expensive)

1. `./tlua check --format=json` — fix `error` entries only (`warning` never fails the build).
2. Re-run the one failing file with `tlua run --check` for a fast repro.
3. For multi-file inference questions, read `SPEC.md` §3/§11, not LSP hover alone.
4. Keep new snippets minimal, then run `scripts/check_snippets.py` before pushing docs.


<!-- docs/en/07-testing.md -->

# Testing (EN)

`tlua test` is the zero-configuration test runner: it discovers test files,
type-checks the whole project, injects a small assertion module and runs every
named case in isolation. No harness file, no dependencies.

## Write a test

Put files under `tests/` (or name them `*_test.tl` / `*.test.tl`) and return a
table of cases:

```lua
import T from "tlua_test"

local function add(a: number, b: number): number
  return a + b
end

return {
  ["adds numbers"] = function(): void
    T.eq(add(1, 2), 3)
  end,
  ["concatenates strings"] = function(): void
    T.ok("a" < "b")
    T.eq("x" .. "y", "xy")
  end,
  ["rejects bad input"] = function(): void
    T.raises(function(): void
      error("boom")
    end)
  end,
}
```

The `tlua_test` module is injected at `tlua_modules/tlua_test.tl`, so the
import resolves both for the checker and the runtime.

## Run

```bash
tlua test                              # discover + type-check + run (embedded golua)
tlua test tests/test_store.tl          # explicit files or directories
tlua test --filter compaction          # module or case name contains "compaction"
tlua test --format=json                # one JSON object per line
tlua test --lua lua5.4                 # stock Lua 5.4
tlua test --lua luajit --target 5.1    # LuaJIT build
```

Output:

```
tlua test · 4 file(s)
  ✓ tests.test_store / adds numbers
  ✗ tests.test_store / rejects bad input
      rejects bad input: expected an error
  ✓ tests.test_store / concatenates strings

2 passed, 1 failed (3 checks)
  ✗ tests.test_store / rejects bad input
```

The process exits `1` when any case fails, so CI needs no wrapper.

## Assertions

| Helper | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `T.eq(actual, expected, label?)` | Strict equality (numbers, strings, tables by identity) |
| `T.eqBytes(actual, expected, label?)` | Same as `eq`, documents binary payload intent |
| `T.ok(cond, label?)` | Truthy check |
| `T.raises(fn, label?)` | `fn` must raise; returns the message |
| `T.fail(message)` | Unconditional failure |

A failed assertion stops its case and is reported with `module / case: message`.
Failure details from assertions are counted as *checks*, so "1160 checks" means
1160 expectations across 23 cases.

## How it works

1. Discover `tests/**/*.tl`, `*_test.tl`, `*.test.tl` (skipping `tlua_modules`,
   `dist`, `testdata`).
2. Load the whole project, so library modules are type-checked and emitted too.
3. Inject `tlua_modules/tlua_test.tl` and a generated root runner that
   `require`s each test module by its dotted project path.
4. Check; abort with diagnostics if the project does not type-check.
5. Emit to a temp directory and execute the runner. Each case runs in `pcall`,
   so one failure does not hide the rest.

## CI recipe

```yaml
- run: tlua check
- run: tlua test
- run: tlua test --lua lua5.4
- run: tlua test --lua luajit --target 5.1
```

`--format=json` is NDJSON: one object per case plus a final
`{"summary":true,...}` line, which is convenient for agents and dashboards.
`tlua test --list --format=json` enumerates cases without running them
(`{"module","case","file"}` per line); the VS Code Test Explorer uses it, and
`--module NAME` / `--case NAME` run exactly one case.


<!-- docs/en/08-examples.md -->

# Examples (EN)

`tlua example` is the cargo-style examples workflow: list what exists, then run
one by name — no paths, no build artifacts.

```bash
tlua example                 # list examples with one-line descriptions
tlua example basic           # run examples/basic.tl or examples/basic/main.tl
tlua example basic -- a b    # pass arguments to the example
tlua example basic --check   # full type check first
tlua example basic --lua lua5.4
```

## Layout

Two layouts are supported and can be mixed:

```
examples/
├── basic.tl          # single-file example
├── batch.tl
└── snapshots/
    └── main.tl       # directory example (main.tl)
```

A directory example wins over a same-named file. Both are listed by name:

```
examples · 3
  basic      Open, write, read, iterate, reopen and clean up.
  batch      Atomic writes with WriteBatch, then a compaction round.
  snapshots  Point-in-time reads: a snapshot ignores later writes.

run one with: tlua example NAME [-- args...]
```

## Descriptions

The first `---` comment line becomes the list description:

```lua
--- Open, write, read, iterate, reopen and clean up.

import leveldb from "leveldb"
-- ...
```

## How running works

The command runs the example through a generated root-level wrapper
(`require("examples.basic")`). Because the wrapper lives at the project root,
the example can import project libraries with normal dotted paths, and the same
entry works with `--lua lua5.4` or `--lua luajit --target 5.1`.

```
examples/basic.tl  ──wrapper──▶  require("examples.basic")
project root on package.path ──▶  import leveldb from "leveldb"
```

## Library examples

`typelua-leveldb` ships its own examples and consumes them exactly this way:

```bash
tlua example              # basic, batch, snapshots
tlua example basic
tlua example batch --lua lua5.4
```

See [Testing](./07-testing) for the companion `tlua test` workflow.


<!-- docs/en/09-debugging.md -->

# Debugging (EN)

`tlua dap` is a Debug Adapter Protocol server. The VS Code extension starts it
automatically; any DAP client can use it over stdio.

## From VS Code

Press `F5` on a `.tl` file, or run **TypeLua: Debug File**. A minimal
`launch.json`:

```json
{
  "type": "typelua",
  "request": "launch",
  "name": "Debug TypeLua",
  "program": "${file}",
  "args": [],
  "stopOnEntry": false,
  "check": false
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `program` | Entry `.tl` file (required) |
| `args` | Script arguments (`arg[1..]`) |
| `cwd` | Working directory (defaults to the workspace folder) |
| `lua` | Interpreter; default auto-detects `lua5.4`, then `luajit` |
| `target` | `5.4` (default) or `5.1` (LuaJIT) |
| `check` | Type-check before running |
| `stopOnEntry` | Break on the first executable line |
| `test` / `testCase` | Debug a test file / a single case |

Breakpoints, step in/over/out, the call stack, locals and program output all
work in the standard Debug view. Positions are mapped from emitted Lua back to
`.tl` lines through the compiler's statement-level source maps.

## Test Explorer

The Testing view lists discovered cases (`tests/**/*.tl`, `*_test.tl`,
`*.test.tl`). The inline ▶ runs a case through `tlua test`; the 🐞 starts a
debug session for it. Pass/fail flows back to the Testing view through a
custom `typelua/testResult` DAP event.

Discovery uses `tlua test --list`:

```bash
tlua test --list --format=json    # {"module","case","file"} per line
```

## How it works

1. Compile the project in memory with mappings (`compiler.Render`).
2. Write the emitted Lua and a debug configuration to a temp directory.
3. Run `dap_agent.lua` under the selected Lua interpreter. The agent installs
   line and call hooks, stops on mapped breakpoints or step conditions, and
   talks to the adapter over stderr (`##tlua-dap` prefix); program output stays
   on stdout.
4. The adapter translates bridge messages to DAP responses/events and maps
   runtime lines back to `.tl` positions.

## Limitations

- **Pause while running** is not implemented; breakpoints set during execution
  apply at the next stop.
- **Evaluate/watch expressions** and **set variable** are not supported.
- The debugger needs an external Lua interpreter (`lua5.4` or `luajit`); the
  embedded `tlua run` runtime has no local-variable inspection.
- FFI programs need `luajit` plus `--target 5.1`.
